penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Becoming a Starlink reseller requires negotiating and maintaining an enterprise reseller agreement, managing hardware provisioning, and handling connectivity SLAs — all per-customer manual work.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: SMB sales for connectivity services at this price point require live discovery calls and account management to close and retain.

rationale: The buyers are SMBs (maritime, construction, remote-site operators) with real connectivity pain and demonstrated willingness to pay — the buyer profile is legitimate. However, operating as a Starlink reseller requires a formal enterprise reseller agreement with SpaceX (gated, non-trivial to obtain), hardware logistics, SLA management, and ongoing account management that cannot be automated. This is a telco/ISP business requiring legal agreements, physical equipment handling, and human sales cycles — entirely outside what a Claude-based factory can build or run. Buildability and autonomy are both near-zero.
solution_plan: No viable solution plan exists for this factory. A Starlink reseller business requires a SpaceX enterprise reseller contract, physical hardware provisioning per site, network SLA management, and B2B sales cycles with live calls and ongoing account management. A solo non-technical operator using Claude cannot build or maintain this. The opportunity is real but belongs to a telco integrator or managed-connectivity provider, not an AI-first micro-services factory.
notes: operational_autonomy=1 and buildability_with_ai=2 both fail build_gates; total after penalties is effectively disqualifying.
